census_structural_lemma_NEW.statement: If M_0,M_1,M_2 are pairwise disjoint perfect matchings of K_8 whose three pairwise unions are all Hamiltonian 8-cycles, then some perfect matching of K_8 has signature (2,1,1) across them -- i.e. (C) implies not (D).
census_structural_lemma_NEW.proof: Step 1: if M_2 uses a distance-3 chord of C = M_0 u M_1 then one of the four adjacent M_0-pairs (resp. M_1-pairs) completes to a (2,1,1) matching. Step 2: otherwise M_2 joins only same-parity vertices, so M_2 = P_E u P_O; M_0 u M_2 Hamiltonian iff P_E != P_O and M_1 u M_2 Hamiltonian iff shift^-1(P_E) != P_O (shift: alpha<->gamma, beta fixed); the four survivors (alpha,beta),(beta,alpha),(beta,gamma),(gamma,beta) each carry an explicit (2,1,1) matching.
census_structural_lemma_NEW.machine_check: both steps verified on all 16,800 nh=3 triples: 13,440 by Step 1, 3,360 by Step 2, 0 counterexamples
census_structural_lemma_NEW.significance: upgrades W27-D3's 32,970-case exhaustion to a short structural lemma
